title: fix(types): derive the user-filter field shape from the spec, declare the container a dialect
body:
Part of objectui#7265 — the `@object-ui/types` slice. Three groups remain in the
gate's `DEBT` block, so this PR deliberately carries no closing keyword.

## The two names, and why they went different ways

`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` declared two schemas under names
`@objectstack/spec/ui` already exports. They were triaged by **reading their
sites**, not by one policy for the group, and the two answers differ.

### BOUND — `UserFilterFieldSchema`

It is the spec's own concept under the spec's own name. Re-measured against the
**RESOLVED** pin `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` (not the 17.2.0 the seeding card
asserted against — byte-identical is a statement about a version, not a
property), the two shapes already agreed on `field`, `type`, `showCount` and
`defaultValues`, the five-member control-type enum included.

Those four now flow in from the spec **by reference** through this package's
import boundary (`stripImportedDefaults`), so the mirror tracks the protocol
instead of drifting. Two divergences are kept and **confined to the members that
carry them**, documented at the declaration:

1. **`label` stays a plain string.** The spec widened it to an i18n union, and
   `@object-ui/plugin-list`'s `UserFilters` renders this key as a React **child**
   (the filter badge reads `f.label || f.field` straight into JSX). A record
   arriving there is not a translated label, it is "Objects are not valid as a
   React child".
2. **`options[]` keeps this package's element**, for the same reason on its own
   `label`.

`.strip()` restores the object's posture rather than inheriting the spec's
`.strict()`: closing this lane would turn a key an author writes today into a
422, which is a protocol decision about the userFilters surface and not a side
effect a burn-down may make.

### WAIVED — `UserFiltersSchema`

A declared dialect, now waived in the gate's `ALLOW` map with its reason instead
of sitting untriaged. Three divergences keep it unbindable, each measured at
17.4.0 and each probed **in both directions** by the new ratchet:

| | this mirror | `@objectstack/spec/ui` |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | required; `dropdown` or `tabs` only (ADR-0053) | defaulted to `dropdown`; keeps `toggle` so shipped configs keep rendering (ADR-0047 3.4a) |
| `tabs` | accepts the legacy `{ id, filters, default }` preset shape `normalizeTabPresets` still normalises at runtime | strict `ViewTabSchema`, `name` required — rejects those documents |
| unknown keys | stripped | rejected |

Binding it would reject metadata that renders today.

## Ledger before / after

Read from the gate's own banner, at the branch point and at this head — the count
is never copied into a comment or a docblock (AGENTS.md #9):

```
before  17 declared dialects, 5 untriaged collisions in 4 packages
after   18 declared dialects, 3 untriaged collisions in 3 packages
```

The `DEBT` block was regenerated with `node scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs --ledger`
and pasted mechanically, never hand-edited. `--claim-ledger` came back
**byte-identical**, so rule 2's block did not move — unlike the `@object-ui/core`
slice, neither declaration touched here carried a spec-alignment claim.

## Clause-2: the published surface did NOT move, measured rather than assumed

The claim comment declares `Clause-2: no`, and the dispatch says to stop and
report if a route moves what this package exports or what an exported type
accepts. It does not, and here is the measurement rather than the assertion:

- **Accept set unchanged.** 108 whole `ListViewSchema` documents parsed through
  the branch-point build and this head's build: **0 divergent**, same success and
  same parsed output on every one, with a lit control proving the comparator can
  report a difference.
- **Exported types unchanged.** A normalised (indent-stripped, sorted) comparison
  of `dist/zod/objectql.zod.d.ts` and `dist/zod/index.zod.d.ts` before and after
  is **empty**. ⚠️ The raw diff is not, and neither is the raw diff of two builds
  of **identical source** — this package's `.d.ts` emit churns union-member order
  between runs, so the raw form is not an instrument here. The same-source
  control is what establishes that.
- **No name enters or leaves the export set** — both declarations are
  module-local, which is why rule 1 had to drop its `export` filter to see them.
- **What DOES move**, declared rather than buried: the four derived members now
  carry the protocol's own `.description` text instead of this package's
  paraphrase, and the emitted runtime code for this one declaration changes.
  Nothing else in the bundle moves.

## Pins that fail before and pass after

Every reading below is from real run output, with the exit code captured by
redirect before any pipe. Each mutation was proven on disk by anchor count **and**
blob hash before any result was read, each restore proven BY STATE (`git diff
HEAD` empty **and** the blob back to HEAD's), and every script carried
`trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute repo-root paths.

- **The import-boundary census caught the new crossing on its own** — the most
  direct before/after pair in this PR, and not one I authored: adding the
  derivation made `imported-defaults-8317.test.ts` red with *"a schema imported by
  a mirror is not in this file's `IMPORTED` list … expected [ 'UserFilterFieldSchema' ]
  to deeply equal []"*. Registering the crossing turns it green (108 → 110 tests).
- **Ablation A — the BIND.** Predicted in writing first: restoring the hand copy
  reds the gate by NAME (fresh, not a stale-ledger message) and reds the
  reference-equality pins, with the waiver half staying green. Observed: gate
  `exit=1`, *"a spec-named symbol is hand-written, not derived: const
  `UserFilterFieldSchema`"*; vitest `exit=1`, **6 failed / 25 passed** — the four
  `is the spec's OWN node, by reference` cases plus the two site cases, and every
  `UserFiltersSchema` case still green.
- **Ablation B — the WAIVER.** Predicted: deleting the `ALLOW` entry reds the gate
  naming `UserFiltersSchema`, which is then in neither map. Observed: gate
  `exit=1` naming it; vitest `exit=1`, **1 failed / 30 passed** — only the `ALLOW`
  assertion, so the bound half is unaffected.
- **Ablation C — the type-level lines really are compiled.** This file's own
  ancestor in this repo once carried type assertions nothing ran
  (objectstack#4074). Falsifying `_labelIsAPlainString` reds
  `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` with `error TS2344: Type 'false' does not satisfy
  the constraint 'true'` at that line; restored and proven by state.
- **Control** — unmutated tree at this head: gate `exit=0`, and the three test
  files green together (141 passed).

## Checks run locally

`check:spec-symbols`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`,
`check:changeset-claims`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:test-path-roots`,
`check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:phantom-deps`,
`check:unused-deps`, `check:readme-exports` (see below), `check:self-import`,
`check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:shell-escape-residue` — all `exit=0` except the
one noted. `check-changeset-presence` and `check-changeset-no-major` `exit=0`.
`type-check:scripts` `exit=0`; `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`
`exit=0` (which chains `tsconfig.test.json`, i.e. the type-level pins).
`check-governed-queue-guard --test` over all six paths: **NOT GOVERNED**.

**NOT MEASURED, declared rather than read as green or red:**
`check:readme-exports` and `check:spec-floors` both `exit=1`, and every finding in
both is the same shape — `no-artifact` / *"not on disk — run `pnpm build` first"*
for packages this branch never touches. That is a whole-workspace-build
precondition this run did not meet, not a red. `@object-ui/types` itself is
**inspected and clean** in the `check:spec-floors` run (18 of 39 published
packages inspected, 137 subpath/symbol pairs judged; it appears in no finding),
and the floor question is answered directly anyway: the declared floor for this
package is `^17.4.0` and the resolved pin **is** 17.4.0, so the newly imported
symbol is present at the floor by construction.

**Lint, narrowed and declared, three readings.** Population = **4987** of 4988
tracked lintable-extension files in scope, read from eslint's own resolved config
via `isPathIgnored`, not guessed. Narrowed run = the 5 changed/added files,
counted from `--format json`: `exit=0`, **0 errors / 1 warning**, and that warning
is a pre-existing `no-explicit-any` in an untouched block of the same file (the
file's `z.any()` count is 28 at the branch point and 28 here). Invariance: this
repo does not enable type-aware linting (`tseslint.configs.recommended`, zero
`parserOptions` / `project` / `projectService` hits in `eslint.config.js`), so
this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. Full farm run left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **noted, not filed:** `.d.ts` emit in `packages/types` is not reproducible
  build-to-build — two builds of byte-identical source differ in union-member and
  object-key order in `dist/zod/index.zod.d.ts` and `dist/zod/objectql.zod.d.ts`.
  It bites any reviewer who diffs `.d.ts` to judge whether a published type moved,
  which is exactly what a Clause-2 measurement does. Not filed because the
  successor is named and is this PR's own reviewer, and because nothing in the
  tree consumes emitted `.d.ts` byte-for-byte today; the normalised comparison
  above is the workaround, and it is written down here rather than left to be
  rediscovered.
- **noted, not filed:** `packages/plugin-list`'s `UserFilters` reads `f.label`
  straight into JSX, so the label narrowing this PR documents is load-bearing
  rather than stylistic. Behaviour is identical before and after this diff —
  binding the shape made the constraint legible, it did not create it. Successor:
  whoever lifts the i18n union into this lane, who now has the reason written at
  the declaration instead of having to rediscover it.
